title: Die wahre Braut
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 186. Text from Wikisource („Die wahre Braut (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly. Contains two blocks of inset verse, four lines each.
about: A stepdaughter is set one impossible task after another — sorting a mountain of feathers in a day, emptying a pond with a leaking spoon — and each time a mysterious old woman appears to do the work for her while she sleeps. When a prince finally takes her for his bride, a false bride is smuggled into her place, and the tale turns on how the true one is recognized and restored.

sentences.t: Es war einmal ein Mädchen, das war jung und schön, aber seine Mutter war ihm früh gestorben, und die Stiefmutter that ihm alles gebrannte Herzeleid an.
sentences.l: There was once a girl, she was young and beautiful, but her mother had died on her early, and the stepmother did her every burning heartache.
sentences.i: There was once a girl who was young and beautiful, but her mother had died when she was small, and the stepmother did her every cruelty she could.
sentences.n: Mädchen is a neuter diminutive, so the German calls the girl es, it, and gives her the possessives sein and ihm right through the tale; English has to say she and her. war ihm gestorben is a dative of interest — died on her, to her loss. alles gebrannte Herzeleid anthun is an old idiom, to do somebody every heartache there is, with gebrannt, burnt, standing as an intensifier.

sentences.t: Wenn sie ihm eine Arbeit auftrug, sie mochte noch so schwer sein, so gieng es unverdrossen daran und that was in seinen Kräften stand.
sentences.l: When she set her a task, it might be ever so hard, she went at it undaunted and did what stood in her powers.
sentences.i: Whenever she set her a task, however hard it might be, she went at it undaunted and did what lay in her power.
sentences.n: eine Arbeit auftragen is to set somebody a task. sie mochte noch so schwer sein is a concessive with no conjunction at all — let it be ever so hard — and English has to supply “however”. was in seinen Kräften stand: what stood in her strength, what lay in her power.

sentences.t: Aber es konnte damit das Herz der bösen Frau nicht rühren, immer war sie unzufrieden, immer war es nicht genug.
sentences.l: But she could not touch the heart of the wicked woman with it; always she was dissatisfied, always it was not enough.
sentences.i: But it never touched the heart of the wicked woman: she was always dissatisfied, it was never enough.
sentences.n: rühren is to stir, to move — das Herz rühren, to touch the heart. The repeated immer … immer, always … always, does the work English does with never.

sentences.t: Je fleißiger es arbeitete, je mehr ward ihm aufgelegt, und sie hatte keinen andern Gedanken, als wie sie ihm eine immer größere Last aufbürden und das Leben recht sauer machen wollte.
sentences.l: The harder she worked, the more was laid on her, and the woman had no other thought than how she might load an ever greater burden on her and make her life thoroughly bitter.
sentences.i: The harder she worked, the more was laid on her, and the woman had no thought but how to heap an ever heavier burden on her and make her life thoroughly bitter.
sentences.n: je … je is the older form of the modern je … desto, the more … the more. ward is the old simple past of werden, here building the passive. das Leben sauer machen is to make life sour, to make it a misery.

sentences.t: Eines Tags sagte sie zu ihm „da hast du zwölf Pfund Federn, die sollst du abschleißen, und wenn du nicht heute Abend damit fertig bist, so wartet eine Tracht Schläge auf dich. Meinst du, du könntest den ganzen Tag faullenzen?“
sentences.l: One day she said to her “there you have twelve pounds of feathers, those you are to strip, and if you are not finished with them this evening, a good beating waits for you. Do you think you could laze the whole day long?”
sentences.i: One day she said to her: “There are twelve pounds of feathers for you, and you are to strip them; and if you are not finished with them by this evening, a beating is waiting for you. Do you think you could idle the whole day away?”
sentences.n: Federn abschleißen is the old household work of stripping the soft down from the quills of feathers for beds and pillows — a job that took whole evenings and was done in company. eine Tracht Schläge is fixed: a load of blows, a good hiding. faullenzen is the 1857 spelling of faulenzen.

sentences.t: Das arme Mädchen setzte sich zu der Arbeit nieder, aber die Thränen flossen ihm dabei über die Wangen herab, denn es sah wohl daß es unmöglich war mit der Arbeit in einem Tage zu Ende zu kommen.
sentences.l: The poor girl set herself down to the work, but the tears ran down over her cheeks the while, for she saw well that it was impossible to come to an end with the work in one day.
sentences.i: The poor girl sat down to the work, but the tears ran down her cheeks as she did it, for she saw well enough that it was impossible to come to the end of it in a single day.
sentences.n: sich niedersetzen, to set oneself down, with nieder at the end. Thränen is the 1857 spelling of Tränen. zu Ende kommen mit is to get to the end of something, to finish it.

sentences.t: Wenn es ein Häufchen Federn vor sich liegen hatte und es seufzte oder schlug in seiner Angst die Hände zusammen, so stoben sie aus einander und es mußte sie wieder auflesen und von neuem anfangen.
sentences.l: When she had a little heap of feathers lying before her and she sighed or struck her hands together in her fear, they flew apart and she had to pick them up again and begin from new.
sentences.i: Whenever she had a little heap of feathers lying in front of her, and sighed, or in her distress clapped her hands together, they scattered, and she had to gather them up and begin all over again.
sentences.n: stoben is the past plural of stieben, to fly apart, to scatter — nothing to do with die Stube, a parlour, though the spelling comes close. die Hände zusammenschlagen is to clap the hands together in dismay. von neuem, afresh.

sentences.t: Da stützte es einmal die Elbogen auf den Tisch, legte sein Gesicht in beide Hände, und rief „ist denn niemand auf Gottes Erdboden, der sich meiner erbarmt?“
sentences.l: Then once she propped her elbows on the table, laid her face in both hands, and cried “is there then nobody on God’s earth who takes pity on me?”
sentences.i: Then once she propped her elbows on the table, laid her face in both her hands, and cried: “Is there nobody on God’s earth who will take pity on me?”
sentences.n: Elbogen is the older spelling of Ellbogen. sich jemandes erbarmen takes the genitive — sich meiner erbarmen, to take pity on me — one of the last places where German still uses a genitive with a verb. denn inside a question is a flavouring word: is there then …

sentences.t: Indem hörte es eine sanfte Stimme, die sprach „tröste dich, mein Kind, ich bin gekommen dir zu helfen.“
sentences.l: Just then she heard a gentle voice, which said “comfort yourself, my child, I have come to help you.”
sentences.i: Just then she heard a gentle voice which said: “Take comfort, my child, I have come to help you.”
sentences.n: indem here means just then, at that moment, an older use of the word. sich trösten is reflexive in German where English is not: to take comfort. helfen takes the dative, dir zu helfen.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen blickte auf, und eine alte Frau stand neben ihm.
sentences.l: The girl looked up, and an old woman stood beside her.
sentences.n: aufblicken, to look up, with auf at the end: blickte … auf. neben ihm — ihm, because Mädchen is neuter, and it is the girl who is meant.

sentences.t: Sie faßte das Mädchen freundlich an der Hand, und sprach „vertraue mir nur an was dich drückt.“
sentences.l: She took the girl kindly by the hand, and said “only confide in me what presses on you.”
sentences.i: She took the girl kindly by the hand and said: “Only tell me what is weighing on you.”
sentences.n: anvertrauen, to entrust, to confide, splits: vertraue … an. drücken is to press, to weigh — was dich drückt, what is pressing on you, is ordinary German for a trouble.

sentences.t: Da sie so herzlich sprach, so erzählte ihr das Mädchen von seinem traurigen Leben, daß ihm eine Last auf die andere gelegt würde und es mit den aufgegebenen Arbeiten nicht mehr zu Ende kommen könnte.
sentences.l: Since she spoke so heartily, the girl told her of her sad life, that one burden after another was laid on her and that she could no longer come to the end of the tasks set her.
sentences.i: Since she spoke so kindly, the girl told her of her sad life — how one burden after another was laid on her, and how she could no longer come to the end of the tasks set her.
sentences.n: da at the head of a clause here is because, since, and not then. würde and könnte are both subjunctive, which is how German marks reported speech and keeps the girl’s words hers. aufgegeben, given up, means set, imposed — eine Arbeit aufgeben, to set a task.

sentences.t: „Wenn ich mit diesen Federn heute Abend nicht fertig bin, so schlägt mich die Stiefmutter; sie hat mirs angedroht, und ich weiß sie hält Wort.“
sentences.l: “If I am not finished with these feathers this evening, the stepmother beats me; she has threatened me with it, and I know she keeps her word.”
sentences.i: “If I am not finished with these feathers by this evening, my stepmother will beat me; she has threatened me with it, and I know she keeps her word.”
sentences.n: German uses the plain present, schlägt, where English needs a future, will beat. mirs is mir es run together: threatened it to me. Wort halten, to keep one’s word, takes no article.

sentences.t: Ihre Thränen fiengen wieder an zu fließen, aber die gute Alte sprach „sei unbesorgt, mein Kind, ruhe dich aus, ich will derweil deine Arbeit verrichten.“
sentences.l: Her tears began again to flow, but the good old woman said “be untroubled, my child, rest yourself, I will do your work meanwhile.”
sentences.i: Her tears began to flow again, but the good old woman said: “Be easy, my child, rest yourself; I will do your work in the meantime.”
sentences.n: fiengen … an is anfangen with its particle at the end. die Alte is the old woman — the same adjective-as-noun that gives der Alte, the old man; she has no other name in the tale. derweil, meanwhile, is the older word for the modern inzwischen.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen legte sich auf sein Bett und schlief bald ein.
sentences.l: The girl laid herself on her bed and soon fell asleep.
sentences.i: The girl lay down on her bed and soon fell asleep.
sentences.n: einschlafen, to fall asleep, with ein at the end: schlief … ein. sein Bett is her bed — the neuter possessive following Mädchen again.

sentences.t: Die Alte setzte sich an den Tisch bei die Federn, hu! wie flogen sie von den Kielen ab, die sie mit ihren dürren Händen kaum berührte.
sentences.l: The old woman set herself at the table by the feathers — hu! how they flew off from the quills, which she barely touched with her withered hands.
sentences.i: The old woman sat down at the table by the feathers — and my, how they flew off the quills, which she barely touched with her withered hands.
sentences.n: hu! is a cry of astonishment thrown into the narration, as though the teller were watching it happen. bei die Federn takes the accusative where modern German would have the dative bei den Federn; the 1857 text keeps the older usage. abfliegen, to fly off, splits: flogen … ab.

sentences.t: Bald war sie mit den zwölf Pfund fertig.
sentences.l: Soon she was finished with the twelve pounds.
sentences.n: Pfund stays singular after a numeral, as German measures do: zwölf Pfund, twelve pound.

sentences.t: Als das Mädchen erwachte, lagen große schneeweiße Haufen aufgethürmt, und alles war im Zimmer reinlich aufgeräumt, aber die Alte war verschwunden.
sentences.l: When the girl awoke, great snow-white heaps lay piled up, and everything in the room was cleanly tidied, but the old woman had vanished.
sentences.i: When the girl awoke, great snow-white heaps lay piled up, and everything in the room was neatly cleared away — but the old woman had vanished.
sentences.n: aufgethürmt is the 1857 spelling of aufgetürmt, from aufthürmen, to pile up like a tower. The helper never stays to be thanked, and she leaves the same way all three times.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen dankte Gott und saß still bis der Abend kam.
sentences.l: The girl thanked God and sat still until the evening came.
sentences.n: danken takes the dative: dankte Gott, thanked God. still sitzen, to sit quiet — she does not go and find the stepmother, which is why the next sentence has to bring the stepmother to her.

sentences.t: Da trat die Stiefmutter herein und staunte über die vollbrachte Arbeit.
sentences.l: Then the stepmother stepped in and was astonished at the accomplished work.
sentences.i: Then the stepmother came in, and was astonished at the work accomplished.
sentences.n: hereintreten, to step in, with herein at the end. staunen über, to be astonished at. vollbracht, from vollbringen, is a lofty word for finished, accomplished.

sentences.t: „Siehst du, Trulle,“ sprach sie, „was man ausrichtet, wenn man fleißig ist? hättest du nicht noch etwas anderes vornehmen können? aber da sitzest du und legst die Hände in den Schooß.“
sentences.l: “Do you see, you slattern,” said she, “what one accomplishes when one is diligent? could you not have taken up something else besides? but there you sit and lay your hands in your lap.”
sentences.i: “Do you see, you slattern,” said she, “what one gets done by being diligent? Could you not have taken up something else as well? But there you sit with your hands in your lap.”
sentences.n: Trulle is a coarse word for a woman, a slattern or a drab, and the stepmother is being deliberately foul. ausrichten is to get done, to accomplish. vornehmen here is the verb, to take up, to set about, not the adjective vornehm, of high rank. die Hände in den Schooß legen is the German picture of idleness, and Schooß is the 1857 spelling of Schoß.

sentences.t: Als sie hinausgieng, sprach sie, „die Creatur kann mehr als Brot essen, ich muß ihr schwerere Arbeit auflegen.“
sentences.l: As she went out, she said, “the creature can do more than eat bread, I must lay heavier work on her.”
sentences.i: As she went out she said: “The creature can do more than eat bread — I must set her heavier work.”
sentences.n: Creatur is the 1857 spelling of Kreatur, and it is contemptuous: the creature, the thing. mehr als Brot essen können is an old saying for being good for more than merely feeding oneself. eine Arbeit auflegen is to lay work on somebody, to impose it.

sentences.t: Am andern Morgen rief sie das Mädchen und sprach „da hast du einen Löffel, damit schöpfe mir den großen Teich aus, der bei dem Garten liegt. Und wenn du damit Abends nicht zu Rand gekommen bist, so weißt du was erfolgt.“
sentences.l: On the next morning she called the girl and said “there you have a spoon, with it scoop me out the great pond that lies by the garden. And if you have not come to the edge of it by evening, you know what follows.”
sentences.i: Next morning she called the girl and said: “There is a spoon for you; with it you are to bail out the great pond that lies by the garden. And if you have not got to the end of it by evening, you know what follows.”
sentences.n: der andere Morgen is the next morning, not another one. ausschöpfen, to scoop or bail out, splits: schöpfe … aus. zu Rand kommen mit is an old phrase, to come to the edge of a thing, to get to the end of it. Abends is a genitive of time used as an adverb, of an evening.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen nahm den Löffel und sah daß er durchlöchert war, und wenn er es auch nicht gewesen wäre, es hätte nimmermehr damit den Teich ausgeschöpft.
sentences.l: The girl took the spoon and saw that it was riddled with holes, and even if it had not been so, she would never have bailed the pond out with it.
sentences.i: The girl took the spoon and saw that it was full of holes; and even if it had not been, she could never have bailed out the pond with it.
sentences.n: wenn er es auch nicht gewesen wäre is a concessive subjunctive: even if it had not been. er is the spoon, masculine, where English must say it. nimmermehr, nevermore, never in the world.

sentences.t: Es machte sich gleich an die Arbeit, kniete am Wasser, in das seine Thränen fielen, und schöpfte.
sentences.l: She set herself at once to the work, knelt by the water, into which her tears fell, and scooped.
sentences.i: She set to work at once, knelt at the water, into which her tears were falling, and scooped.
sentences.n: sich an die Arbeit machen, to set to work. The relative clause in das seine Thränen fielen sits inside the sentence and the main verb schöpfte waits behind it; the tears fall into the pond she is trying to empty, and the German lets that stand without a word of comment.

sentences.t: Aber die gute Alte erschien wieder, und als sie die Ursache von seinem Kummer erfuhr, sprach sie „sei getrost, mein Kind, geh in das Gebüsch und lege dich schlafen, ich will deine Arbeit schon thun.“
sentences.l: But the good old woman appeared again, and when she learned the cause of her grief, she said “be of good cheer, my child, go into the bushes and lay yourself down to sleep, I will do your work well enough.”
sentences.i: But the good old woman appeared again, and when she learned the cause of her grief she said: “Be of good cheer, my child; go into the bushes and lie down to sleep — I shall do your work for you.”
sentences.n: erfahren is to learn, to come to know, not to experience. schon in ich will deine Arbeit schon thun is a flavouring word of reassurance: never fear, I shall do it. thun is the 1857 spelling of tun.

sentences.t: Als die Alte allein war, berührte sie nur den Teich: wie ein Dunst stieg das Wasser in die Höhe und vermischte sich mit den Wolken.
sentences.l: When the old woman was alone, she only touched the pond: like a vapour the water rose up into the height and mingled itself with the clouds.
sentences.i: When the old woman was alone she merely touched the pond: like a mist the water rose into the air and mingled with the clouds.
sentences.n: nur berühren — she only touches it, and the colon does the rest, where English might want an “and at once”. in die Höhe steigen, to rise up. sich vermischen mit, to mingle with.

sentences.t: Allmählig ward der Teich leer, und als das Mädchen vor Sonnenuntergang erwachte und herbeikam, so sah es nur noch die Fische, die in dem Schlamm zappelten.
sentences.l: Gradually the pond grew empty, and when the girl awoke before sundown and came up, she saw only the fish still, which were floundering in the mud.
sentences.i: Little by little the pond grew empty, and when the girl awoke before sundown and came up, she saw nothing left but the fish floundering in the mud.
sentences.n: Allmählig is the 1857 spelling of allmählich. nur noch is only still, nothing left but. zappeln is to flounder, to thrash about — the one hard picture in a tale otherwise full of splendour.

sentences.t: Es gieng zu der Stiefmutter und zeigte ihr an daß die Arbeit vollbracht wäre.
sentences.l: She went to the stepmother and announced to her that the work was accomplished.
sentences.i: She went to the stepmother and told her that the work was done.
sentences.n: anzeigen, to announce, to report, is a formal word, and its particle an waits at the end: zeigte … an. wäre is subjunctive because the report is hers and not the narrator’s.

sentences.t: „Du hättest längst fertig sein sollen,“ sagte sie und ward blaß vor Ärger, aber sie sann etwas Neues aus.
sentences.l: “You ought to have been finished long ago,” said she and grew pale with rage, but she thought out something new.
sentences.i: “You ought to have been finished long ago,” said she, and grew pale with rage; but she thought out something new.
sentences.n: hättest … sein sollen is the double infinitive German uses in the perfect of a modal: ought to have been. vor with an emotion gives its cause — vor Ärger, with rage. aussinnen, to think out, to devise, with aus at the end.

sentences.t: Am dritten Morgen sprach sie zu dem Mädchen „dort in der Ebene mußt du mir ein schönes Schloß bauen und zum Abend muß es fertig sein.“
sentences.l: On the third morning she said to the girl “there on the plain you must build me a fine castle, and by evening it must be finished.”
sentences.i: On the third morning she said to the girl: “Out there on the plain you must build me a fine castle, and by evening it must be finished.”
sentences.n: mir here is a dative of interest: build me a castle, for my use. zum Abend, by evening. The three tasks rise in impossibility — feathers, a pond, a castle — as they always do in these tales.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen erschrack und sagte „wie kann ich ein so großes Werk vollbringen?“
sentences.l: The girl took fright and said “how can I accomplish so great a work?”
sentences.n: erschrack is the 1857 spelling of erschrak, from erschrecken, to take fright. vollbringen, to accomplish, is the same lofty verb as vollbracht two sentences before.

sentences.t: „Ich dulde keinen Widerspruch,“ schrie die Stiefmutter, „kannst du mit einem durchlöcherten Löffel einen Teich ausschöpfen, so kannst du auch ein Schloß bauen. Noch heute will ich es beziehen, und wenn etwas fehlt, sei es das geringste in Küche oder Keller, so weißt du was dir bevorsteht.“
sentences.l: “I tolerate no contradiction,” cried the stepmother, “if you can bail out a pond with a spoon full of holes, you can build a castle too. This very day I mean to move into it, and if anything is missing, be it the least thing in kitchen or cellar, you know what lies before you.”
sentences.i: “I will hear no contradiction,” cried the stepmother. “If you can bail out a pond with a spoon full of holes, you can build a castle too. This very day I mean to move in; and if anything is wanting, be it the least thing in kitchen or cellar, you know what is in store for you.”
sentences.n: dulde is the first person present, I tolerate, and not an imperative. beziehen here is to move into a house — the same verb turns up later in the tale meaning to cover, of walls hung with silk. sei es is a subjunctive of concession, be it, even if it be. bevorstehen, to lie ahead, to be in store.

sentences.t: Sie trieb das Mädchen fort, und als es in das Thal kam, so lagen da die Felsen über einander aufgethürmt; mit aller seiner Kraft konnte es den kleinsten nicht einmal bewegen.
sentences.l: She drove the girl off, and when she came into the valley, there lay the rocks piled one over another; with all her strength she could not even move the smallest.
sentences.i: She drove the girl off, and when she came down into the valley, there lay the rocks piled one upon another; with all her strength she could not stir even the smallest of them.
sentences.n: forttreiben, to drive off, splits: trieb … fort. Thal is the 1857 spelling of Tal. nicht einmal is not even; einmal by itself would be once.

sentences.t: Es setzte sich nieder und weinte, doch hoffte es auf den Beistand der guten Alten.
sentences.l: She set herself down and wept, yet she hoped for the help of the good old woman.
sentences.i: She sat down and wept, yet she hoped for the good old woman’s help.
sentences.n: hoffen auf takes the accusative: to hope for. der guten Alten is genitive, of the good old woman — the adjective-as-noun still declining like an adjective.

sentences.t: Sie ließ auch nicht lange auf sich warten, kam und sprach ihm Trost ein, „lege dich nur dort in den Schatten, und schlaf, ich will dir das Schloß schon bauen. Wenn es dir Freude macht, so kannst du selbst darin wohnen.“
sentences.l: Nor did she let herself be waited for long: she came and spoke comfort into her, “only lay yourself down there in the shade, and sleep, I will build you the castle well enough. If it gives you pleasure, you can live in it yourself.”
sentences.i: Nor did she keep her waiting long: she came and spoke comfort to her. “Only lie down there in the shade and sleep; I shall build you the castle. If it pleases you, you can live in it yourself.”
sentences.n: auf sich warten lassen, to keep somebody waiting, is a fixed phrase. jemandem Trost einsprechen is an old idiom, to speak comfort into somebody, with the particle ein at the end. Freude machen, to give pleasure. Her last sentence is the first hint that the castle will end up the girl’s.

sentences.t: Als das Mädchen weggegangen war, rührte die Alte die grauen Felsen an.
sentences.l: When the girl had gone away, the old woman touched the grey rocks.
sentences.n: anrühren, to touch, with an at the end: rührte … an. weggehen takes sein in the perfect, war weggegangen, as verbs of motion do.

sentences.t: Alsbald regten sie sich, rückten zusammen und standen da, als hätten Riesen die Mauer gebaut: darauf erhob sich das Gebäude, und es war als ob unzählige Hände unsichtbar arbeiteten und Stein auf Stein legten.
sentences.l: At once they stirred, moved together and stood there as if giants had built the wall: thereupon the building rose up, and it was as though countless hands were working unseen and laying stone on stone.
sentences.i: At once they stirred, moved together and stood there as though giants had built the wall; thereupon the building rose up, and it was as if countless hands were working unseen and laying stone upon stone.
sentences.n: sich regen, to stir. als hätten … gebaut and als ob … arbeiteten are both subjunctives of comparison, as if; German can drop the ob and simply invert the verb, als hätten Riesen. darauf here is thereupon, of time, not of place.

sentences.t: Der Boden dröhnte, große Seulen stiegen von selbst in die Höhe und stellten sich neben einander in Ordnung.
sentences.l: The ground boomed, great pillars rose of themselves into the height and set themselves beside one another in order.
sentences.i: The ground boomed; great pillars rose of themselves into the air and ranged themselves side by side in order.
sentences.n: Seulen is the 1857 spelling of Säulen, pillars. von selbst is of their own accord. sich stellen, to place oneself — everything in this passage does its own work, and the German keeps every verb reflexive to say so.

sentences.t: Auf dem Dach legten sich die Ziegeln zurecht, und als es Mittag war, drehte sich schon die große Wetterfahne wie eine goldene Jungfrau mit fliegendem Gewand auf der Spitze des Thurms.
sentences.l: On the roof the tiles laid themselves into place, and when it was midday, the great weather-vane was already turning like a golden maiden with flying robe on the point of the tower.
sentences.i: On the roof the tiles laid themselves in place, and by midday the great weather-vane was already turning, like a golden maiden with her robe flying, on the point of the tower.
sentences.n: sich zurechtlegen, to lay oneself into place, with zurecht at the end. Thurms is the 1857 spelling of Turms. mit fliegendem Gewand is a bare dative with no article, as German leaves such descriptive phrases.

sentences.t: Das Innere des Schlosses war bis zum Abend vollendet.
sentences.l: The inside of the castle was completed by evening.
sentences.n: das Innere is an adjective made into a neuter noun, the inner part, and it still declines like an adjective. bis zum Abend, by evening.

sentences.t: Wie es die Alte anfieng, weiß ich nicht, aber die Wände der Zimmer waren mit Seide und Sammet bezogen,
sentences.l: How the old woman went about it, I do not know, but the walls of the rooms were hung with silk and velvet,
sentences.i: How the old woman managed it I do not know, but the walls of the rooms were hung with silk and velvet,
sentences.n: es anfangen is to go about a thing, to set about it. weiß ich nicht — the teller steps into the tale for one clause and then out of it again, something the Grimms’ narrators do very rarely. Sammet is the older spelling of Samt, velvet, and bezogen here means covered, hung, not moved into.

sentences.t: buntgestickte Stühle standen da und reichverzierte Armsessel an Tischen von Marmor, krystallne Kronleuchter hiengen von der Bühne herab und spiegelten sich in dem glatten Boden:
sentences.l: brightly embroidered chairs stood there and richly ornamented armchairs at tables of marble, crystal chandeliers hung down from the ceiling and were mirrored in the smooth floor:
sentences.i: brightly embroidered chairs stood there, and richly ornamented armchairs at tables of marble; crystal chandeliers hung down from the ceiling and were mirrored in the smooth floor:
sentences.n: Bühne here is not a stage but the ceiling, the boarded loft over a room — an older and regional sense of the word. krystallne is a contracted krystallene, crystal; hiengen is the 1857 spelling of hingen. sich spiegeln, to be mirrored.

sentences.t: grüne Papageien saßen in goldenen Käfigen und fremde Vögel, die lieblich sangen:
sentences.l: green parrots sat in golden cages, and strange birds that sang sweetly:
sentences.n: fremd is both strange and foreign; these are birds from far off, and they will be heard once more in the last sentence of the tale. The colon runs straight on into the next clause, as this whole inventory does.

sentences.t: überall war eine Pracht, als wenn ein König da einziehen sollte.
sentences.l: everywhere was a splendour, as if a king were to move in there.
sentences.i: everywhere there was such splendour as if a king were about to move in.
sentences.n: als wenn with a subjunctive is as if. einziehen, to move in, is the verb the stepmother will use of herself a few lines later; the tale has already told the reader who is not going to live here.

sentences.t: Die Sonne wollte eben untergehen, als das Mädchen erwachte und ihm der Glanz von tausend Lichtern entgegen leuchtete.
sentences.l: The sun was just about to go down when the girl awoke and the radiance of a thousand lights shone toward her.
sentences.i: The sun was just going down when the girl awoke, and the radiance of a thousand lights shone out to meet her.
sentences.n: wollte eben untergehen — wollen here is not to want but to be on the point of. entgegen leuchten, to shine toward somebody, is printed as two words in 1857 and takes the dative, ihm.

sentences.t: Mit schnellen Schritten kam es heran und trat durch das geöffnete Thor in das Schloß.
sentences.l: With quick steps she came up and stepped through the opened gate into the castle.
sentences.i: With quick steps she came up and stepped through the open gate into the castle.
sentences.n: herankommen, to come up, to approach, with heran at the end. Thor is the 1857 spelling of Tor, a gate.

sentences.t: Die Treppe war mit rothem Tuch belegt und das goldene Geländer mit blühenden Bäumen besetzt.
sentences.l: The staircase was laid with red cloth and the golden banister set with flowering trees.
sentences.i: The staircase was laid with red cloth, and the golden banister set about with flowering trees.
sentences.n: rothem is the 1857 spelling of rotem. belegen and besetzen make a pair — to lay over and to set about — and the second clause leaves its verb to be understood from the first: das Geländer [war] besetzt.

sentences.t: Als es die Pracht der Zimmer erblickte, blieb es wie erstarrt stehen.
sentences.l: When she caught sight of the splendour of the rooms, she stayed standing as if turned to stone.
sentences.i: When she caught sight of the splendour of the rooms, she stood still as though turned to stone.
sentences.n: stehen bleiben, to stop, to stand still. erstarrt, from erstarren, is to grow stiff, to freeze — the German says rigid where English says turned to stone.

sentences.t: Wer weiß wie lang es so gestanden hätte, wenn ihm nicht der Gedanke an die Stiefmutter gekommen wäre.
sentences.l: Who knows how long she would have stood so, if the thought of the stepmother had not come to her.
sentences.i: Who knows how long she would have stood there, if the thought of her stepmother had not come to her.
sentences.n: hätte … gestanden and wäre … gekommen are both past subjunctives, the German for what would have happened. der Gedanke an is the thought of; German uses an, at, where English uses of.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ sprach es zu sich selbst, „wenn sie doch endlich zufrieden gestellt wäre und mir das Leben nicht länger zur Qual machen wollte.“
sentences.l: “Ah,” she said to herself, “if only she were satisfied at last and would no longer make my life a torment to me.”
sentences.i: “Ah,” she said to herself, “if only she were satisfied at last, and would make my life a torment to me no longer.”
sentences.n: wenn … doch with a subjunctive and no main clause is a wish left hanging: if only. zufrieden stellen, to satisfy. zur Qual machen, to turn into a torment.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen gieng und zeigte ihr an daß das Schloß fertig wäre.
sentences.l: The girl went and announced to her that the castle was finished.
sentences.n: The same anzeigen and the same subjunctive wäre as after the pond: the tale repeats its own sentences deliberately, and that repetition is how three separate tasks are felt as one shape.

sentences.t: „Gleich will ich einziehen“ sagte sie und erhob sich von ihrem Sitz.
sentences.l: “At once I will move in,” said she and raised herself from her seat.
sentences.i: “I shall move in at once,” said she, and rose from her seat.
sentences.n: Sitz here is the noun, a seat, and not an imperative of any verb. sich erheben, to raise oneself, to rise.

sentences.t: Als sie in das Schloß eintrat, mußte sie die Hand vor die Augen halten, so blendete sie der Glanz.
sentences.l: When she stepped into the castle, she had to hold her hand before her eyes, so did the radiance dazzle her.
sentences.i: When she stepped into the castle she had to hold her hand before her eyes, so much did the radiance dazzle her.
sentences.n: so blendete sie der Glanz inverts the verb to give a result: so greatly did the radiance dazzle her. die Hand — the plain article again where English says her hand.

sentences.t: „Siehst du,“ sagte sie zu dem Mädchen, „wie leicht dirs geworden ist, ich hätte dir etwas Schwereres aufgeben sollen.“
sentences.l: “Do you see,” said she to the girl, “how easy it has come to you; I ought to have set you something harder.”
sentences.i: “Do you see,” said she to the girl, “how easily it came to you? I ought to have set you something harder.”
sentences.n: dirs is dir es. es wird einem leicht is an impersonal turn: it comes easily to one. aufgeben, to set a task, is the same verb the girl used in her complaint to the old woman.

sentences.t: Sie gieng durch alle Zimmer und spürte in allen Ecken ob etwas fehlte oder mangelhaft wäre, aber sie konnte nichts auffinden.
sentences.l: She went through all the rooms and searched in every corner whether anything were missing or defective, but she could find nothing.
sentences.i: She went through all the rooms and searched every corner to see whether anything was missing or wanting, but she could find nothing.
sentences.n: spüren here is to search, to track — the hunter’s word, in an older use. ob etwas fehlte oder mangelhaft wäre is subjunctive again, because it is what she was looking for and not what was so.

sentences.t: „Jetzt wollen wir hinabsteigen,“ sprach sie und sah das Mädchen mit boshaften Blicken an, „Küche und Keller muß noch untersucht werden, und hast du etwas vergessen, so sollst du deiner Strafe nicht entgehen.“
sentences.l: “Now let us go down,” said she and looked at the girl with malicious looks, “kitchen and cellar must still be examined, and if you have forgotten anything, you shall not escape your punishment.”
sentences.i: “Now let us go down,” said she, and looked at the girl with malicious eyes. “Kitchen and cellar have still to be examined, and if you have forgotten anything you shall not escape your punishment.”
sentences.n: wollen wir is a first person plural invitation, let us. ansehen, to look at, with an at the end: sah … an. hast du etwas vergessen with no wenn is a condition made by inversion alone: if you have forgotten anything. entgehen takes the dative, deiner Strafe entgehen.

sentences.t: Aber das Feuer brannte auf dem Herd, in den Töpfen kochten die Speisen, Kluft und Schippe waren angelehnt, und an den Wänden das blanke Geschirr von Messing aufgestellt.
sentences.l: But the fire was burning on the hearth, in the pots the dishes were cooking, tongs and shovel were leaning ready, and along the walls the bright brass vessels set out.
sentences.i: But the fire was burning on the hearth, the food was cooking in the pots, tongs and shovel stood leaning ready, and along the walls the bright brass vessels were set out.
sentences.n: Kluft here is not a chasm but the fire-tongs, a regional (Hessian) word standing beside Schippe, the shovel; the pair is hearth gear and belongs together. angelehnt is leaned up against something — the word comes back three sentences later, of the trapdoor, and that is where the plot turns. The last clause leaves out its verb: [war] aufgestellt.

sentences.t: Nichts fehlte, selbst nicht der Kohlenkasten und die Wassereimer.
sentences.l: Nothing was missing, not even the coal-box and the water-buckets.
sentences.n: selbst nicht is not even. The inventory ends on the two dullest objects in a kitchen, which is the joke: the old woman has furnished the castle down to the coal-box.

sentences.t: „Wo ist der Eingang zum Keller?“ rief sie, „wo der nicht mit Weinfässern reichlich angefüllt ist, so wird dirs schlimm ergehen.“
sentences.l: “Where is the entrance to the cellar?” she cried, “if that is not richly filled with wine-casks, it will go badly with you.”
sentences.i: “Where is the entrance to the cellar?” she cried. “If that is not well filled with wine-casks, it will go badly with you.”
sentences.n: The second wo is not where but if — an older conditional use: wo der nicht … angefüllt ist, if it is not filled. es ergeht einem schlimm is impersonal, it goes badly with one.

sentences.t: Sie hob selbst die Fallthüre auf und stieg die Treppe hinab, aber kaum hatte sie zwei Schritte gethan, so stürzte die schwere Fallthüre, die nur angelehnt war, nieder.
sentences.l: She lifted the trapdoor up herself and went down the stairs, but scarcely had she taken two steps when the heavy trapdoor, which was only leaning to, crashed down.
sentences.i: She lifted the trapdoor herself and went down the stairs; but scarcely had she taken two steps when the heavy trapdoor, which had only been propped up, crashed down.
sentences.n: kaum hatte sie … so is a fixed pattern: scarcely had she … when. gethan is the 1857 spelling of getan. angelehnt, only leaning and not fastened, is the same word used of the tongs and shovel three sentences earlier, and here it kills her.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen hörte einen Schrei, hob die Thüre schnell auf, um ihr zu Hilfe zu kommen, aber sie war hinabgestürzt und es fand sie entseelt auf dem Boden liegen.
sentences.l: The girl heard a cry, lifted the door quickly up in order to come to her help, but she had fallen down and she found her lying lifeless on the ground.
sentences.i: The girl heard a cry and lifted the door quickly, to come to her help; but she had fallen, and the girl found her lying lifeless on the ground.
sentences.n: Schrei here is the noun, a cry. entseelt, un-souled, is a lofty word for dead. The tale does not pause over the death, and the girl’s first act is to try to save her — that too is left without comment.

sentences.t: Nun gehörte das prächtige Schloß dem Mädchen ganz allein.
sentences.l: Now the splendid castle belonged to the girl quite alone.
sentences.i: Now the splendid castle belonged to the girl alone.
sentences.n: gehören takes the dative, dem Mädchen. ganz allein, entirely alone — the old woman’s offer that she might live in it herself has come true in a way nobody said aloud.

sentences.t: Es wußte sich in der ersten Zeit gar nicht in seinem Glück zu finden, schöne Kleider hiengen in den Schränken, die Truhen waren mit Gold und Silber oder mit Perlen und Edelsteinen angefüllt, und es hatte keinen Wunsch, den es nicht erfüllen konnte.
sentences.l: She did not know how to find herself in her good fortune at first at all; beautiful clothes hung in the cupboards, the chests were filled with gold and silver or with pearls and precious stones, and she had no wish that she could not fulfil.
sentences.i: At first she did not know what to make of her good fortune: beautiful clothes hung in the cupboards, the chests were filled with gold and silver, or with pearls and precious stones, and she had no wish she could not fulfil.
sentences.n: sich in etwas finden is to find one’s way in something, to take it in; sich nicht zu finden wissen, not to know what to make of it. gar nicht is not at all. hiengen is the 1857 spelling of hingen.

sentences.t: Bald gieng der Ruf von der Schönheit und dem Reichthum des Mädchens durch die ganze Welt.
sentences.l: Soon the report of the beauty and the wealth of the girl went through the whole world.
sentences.i: Soon the report of the girl’s beauty and wealth went through the whole world.
sentences.n: der Ruf geht is the report goes, spreads. Reichthum is the 1857 spelling of Reichtum. The genitive des Mädchens comes at the end where English puts its possessive at the front.

sentences.t: Alle Tage meldeten sich Freier, aber keiner gefiel ihr.
sentences.l: Every day suitors announced themselves, but not one pleased her.
sentences.i: Every day suitors presented themselves, but not one of them pleased her.
sentences.n: sich melden is to announce oneself, to present oneself. gefallen puts the person pleased in the dative: keiner gefiel ihr, not one was pleasing to her. From this sentence on the tale calls the girl sie and ihr, not es and ihm — she has stopped being das Mädchen for a while.

sentences.t: Endlich kam auch der Sohn eines Königs, der ihr Herz zu rühren wußte, und sie verlobte sich mit ihm.
sentences.l: At last there came also the son of a king, who knew how to touch her heart, and she betrothed herself to him.
sentences.i: At last there came the son of a king who knew how to touch her heart, and she betrothed herself to him.
sentences.n: zu rühren wußte — wissen with an infinitive is to know how to do a thing. sich verloben mit, to become betrothed to. The tale calls him der Sohn eines Königs here and der Königssohn from now on.

sentences.t: In dem Schloßgarten stand eine grüne Linde, darunter saßen sie eines Tages vertraulich zusammen, da sagte er zu ihr „ich will heimziehen und die Einwilligung meines Vaters zu unserer Vermählung holen;
sentences.l: In the castle garden stood a green linden, under it they sat one day close together, and then he said to her “I will go home and fetch my father’s consent to our marriage;
sentences.i: In the castle garden stood a green linden tree, and under it they sat one day in close talk together, and he said to her: “I will go home and fetch my father’s consent to our marriage;
sentences.n: The linden is the tale’s fixed point: everything that follows is measured against this tree and comes back to it at the end. darunter is under it, the pronoun swallowed into the adverb. vertraulich is intimately, in confidence, of two people sitting close.

sentences.t: ich bitte dich harre mein hier unter dieser Linde, in wenigen Stunden bin ich wieder zurück.“
sentences.l: I beg you, wait for me here under this linden; in a few hours I am back again.”
sentences.i: I beg you, wait for me here under this linden tree; in a few hours I shall be back.”
sentences.n: harre mein is an old imperative with a genitive — harren takes the genitive of what is waited for, so mein is “of me” and not “my”. It is deliberately elevated language, and it is exactly the promise he breaks.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen küßte ihn auf den linken Backen und sprach „bleib mir treu, und laß dich von keiner andern auf diesen Backen küssen. Ich will hier unter der Linde warten bis du wieder zurückkommst.“
sentences.l: The girl kissed him on the left cheek and said “stay true to me, and let no other kiss you on this cheek. I will wait here under the linden until you come back again.”
sentences.i: The girl kissed him on the left cheek and said: “Stay true to me, and let no other woman kiss you on this cheek. I shall wait here under the linden until you come back.”
sentences.n: Backen here is der Backen, the cheek, and not the verb backen, to bake; the word decides the whole ending. laß dich … küssen is the causative lassen: let yourself be kissed. keiner andern is dative, by no other woman.

sentences.t: Das Mädchen blieb unter der Linde sitzen, bis die Sonne untergieng, aber er kam nicht wieder zurück.
sentences.l: The girl stayed sitting under the linden until the sun went down, but he did not come back again.
sentences.i: The girl stayed sitting under the linden until the sun went down, but he did not come back.
sentences.n: sitzen bleiben, to stay sitting, is two words in German and one act. untergieng is the 1857 spelling of unterging, from untergehen, of the sun going down.

sentences.t: Sie saß drei Tage von Morgen bis Abend, und erwartete ihn, aber vergeblich.
sentences.l: She sat three days from morning until evening, and waited for him, but in vain.
sentences.n: erwarten is to await, to expect, and takes a plain object where English needs “wait for”. drei Tage is a bare accusative of duration.

sentences.t: Als er am vierten Tag noch nicht da war, so sagte sie „gewiß ist ihm ein Unglück begegnet, ich will ausgehen und ihn suchen und nicht eher wiederkommen als bis ich ihn gefunden habe.“
sentences.l: When on the fourth day he was still not there, she said “surely a misfortune has met him, I will go out and seek him and not come back sooner than until I have found him.”
sentences.i: When on the fourth day he was still not there, she said: “Some misfortune has surely befallen him. I shall go out and look for him, and not come back until I have found him.”
sentences.n: begegnen takes the dative and means to meet, to befall: ist ihm begegnet, has met him. nicht eher … als bis is a heavy old construction, not sooner than until.

sentences.t: Sie packte drei von ihren schönsten Kleidern zusammen, eins mit glänzenden Sternen gestickt, das zweite mit silbernen Monden, das dritte mit goldenen Sonnen, band eine Hand voll Edelsteine in ihr Tuch und machte sich auf.
sentences.l: She packed three of her finest dresses together, one embroidered with shining stars, the second with silver moons, the third with golden suns, tied a handful of precious stones into her cloth and set out.
sentences.i: She packed up three of her finest dresses — one embroidered with shining stars, the second with silver moons, the third with golden suns — tied a handful of jewels into her kerchief, and set out.
sentences.n: zusammenpacken, to pack up, splits: packte … zusammen; sich aufmachen, to set out, likewise: machte sich auf. Star, moon and sun dresses run right through European tales, and here they are the whole of the ending, buried under a stone for years first.

sentences.t: Sie fragte aller Orten nach ihrem Bräutigam, aber niemand hatte ihn gesehen, niemand wußte von ihm.
sentences.l: She asked in all places after her bridegroom, but nobody had seen him, nobody knew of him.
sentences.i: She asked everywhere after her bridegroom, but nobody had seen him, nobody knew of him.
sentences.n: aller Orten is an old genitive plural used as an adverb: in all places, everywhere. nach jemandem fragen, to ask after somebody.

sentences.t: Weit und breit wanderte sie durch die Welt, aber sie fand ihn nicht.
sentences.l: Far and wide she wandered through the world, but she did not find him.
sentences.n: weit und breit, far and wide, is the same pairing in both languages. The sentence is short and flat, and the years it covers are not counted here but two sentences further on.

sentences.t: Endlich vermiethete sie sich bei einem Bauer als Hirtin, und vergrub ihre Kleider und Edelsteine unter einem Stein.
sentences.l: At last she hired herself out to a peasant as a herdswoman, and buried her dresses and precious stones under a stone.
sentences.i: At last she hired herself out to a farmer as a herdswoman, and buried her dresses and jewels under a stone.
sentences.n: sich vermiethen is to hire oneself out, the 1857 spelling of vermieten. Hirtin is the feminine of Hirt, a herdsman; she keeps cattle, as the calf a few lines later shows.

sentences.t: Nun lebte sie als eine Hirtin, hütete ihre Herde, war traurig und voll Sehnsucht nach ihrem Geliebten.
sentences.l: Now she lived as a herdswoman, tended her herd, was sad and full of longing for her beloved.
sentences.i: Now she lived as a herdswoman, tended her herd, and was sad and full of longing for her beloved.
sentences.n: Herde here is die Herde, a herd of cattle, and not der Herd, the hearth — the two words differ by one letter and this tale uses both. Sehnsucht nach, longing for.

sentences.t: Sie hatte ein Kälbchen, das gewöhnte sie an sich, fütterte es aus der Hand, und wenn sie sprach
sentences.l: She had a little calf; that she accustomed to herself, fed it out of her hand, and when she said
sentences.i: She had a little calf, which she made tame to her, feeding it out of her hand; and when she said
sentences.n: an sich gewöhnen is to accustom a creature to oneself, to make it tame. The sentence has no full stop: it runs straight into the verse that follows, which is why the song stands as its own block.

sentences.t:
„Kälbchen, Kälbchen, knie nieder,
vergiß nicht deine Hirtin wieder,
wie der Königssohn die Braut vergaß,
die unter der grünen Linde saß,“
sentences.l:
“Little calf, little calf, kneel down,
forget not your herdswoman again,
as the king’s son forgot the bride
who sat under the green linden,”
sentences.i:
“Little calf, little calf, kneel down,
do not forget your herdswoman,
as the king’s son forgot the bride
who sat beneath the green linden tree,”
sentences.n: The four lines rhyme in pairs in the German — nieder with wieder, vergaß with saß. Lectorium’s idiomatic line does not rhyme, so the sense is given plainly here and the rhyme described instead. niederknien, to kneel down, splits, and nieder ends the first line. wieder in the second line is largely there for the rhyme; the sense is simply do not forget your herdswoman.

sentences.t: so kniete das Kälbchen nieder und ward von ihr gestreichelt.
sentences.l: then the little calf knelt down and was stroked by her.
sentences.n: so picks up the wenn of the sentence before the song: when she said …, then the calf knelt. ward … gestreichelt is the old passive with ward for wurde.

sentences.t: Als sie ein paar Jahre einsam und kummervoll gelebt hatte, so verbreitete sich im Lande das Gerücht, daß die Tochter des Königs ihre Hochzeit feiern wollte.
sentences.l: When she had lived a couple of years lonely and full of grief, the rumour spread in the land that the king’s daughter wanted to celebrate her wedding.
sentences.i: When she had lived a couple of years alone and full of grief, the rumour spread through the land that the king’s daughter was to celebrate her wedding.
sentences.n: sich verbreiten, to spread. wollte here is less wanted than was going to — wollen often carries an intention already settled. The tale gives those years half a clause, and everything since the linden has been passed over.

sentences.t: Der Weg nach der Stadt gieng an dem Dorf vorbei, wo das Mädchen wohnte, und es trug sich zu, als sie einmal ihre Herde austrieb, daß der Bräutigam vorüber zog.
sentences.l: The road to the town went past the village where the girl lived, and it came about, as she once drove out her herd, that the bridegroom passed by.
sentences.i: The road to the town went past the village where the girl lived, and it so happened, as she was once driving out her herd, that the bridegroom came riding past.
sentences.n: vorbeigehen, to go past, splits: gieng … vorbei. sich zutragen is to come about, to happen — an old and rather formal verb. austreiben is to drive cattle out to pasture.

sentences.t: Er saß stolz auf seinem Pferd und sah sie nicht an, aber als sie ihn ansah, so erkannte sie ihren Liebsten.
sentences.l: He sat proudly on his horse and did not look at her, but when she looked at him, she recognised her beloved.
sentences.i: He sat proudly on his horse and did not look at her; but when she looked at him, she knew her beloved.
sentences.n: ansehen, to look at, splits both times — sah … an, ansah — and the two halves of the sentence turn on that one verb. ihren Liebsten is der Liebste, the dearest one, an adjective used as a noun.

sentences.t: Es war als ob ihr ein scharfes Messer in das Herz schnitte.
sentences.l: It was as though a sharp knife were cutting into her heart.
sentences.n: schnitte is the past subjunctive of schneiden, to cut, and not a plural of der Schnitt, a cut. als ob with the subjunctive is as though. ihr … in das Herz is the dative of possession again: into her heart.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ sagte sie, „ich glaubte er wäre mir treu geblieben, aber er hat mich vergessen.“
sentences.l: “Ah,” she said, “I thought he had stayed true to me, but he has forgotten me.”
sentences.n: wäre … geblieben is subjunctive, because it is what she believed and not what was so. treu bleiben takes the dative: mir treu, true to me — the same word she used at the linden.

sentences.t: Am andern Tag kam er wieder des Wegs.
sentences.l: On the next day he came along the way again.
sentences.i: The next day he came along the road again.
sentences.n: des Wegs is a genitive of place used as an adverb, along the way. am andern Tag, on the next day.

sentences.t: Als er in ihrer Nähe war, sprach sie zum Kälbchen,
sentences.l: When he was near her, she said to the little calf,
sentences.n: in jemandes Nähe sein, to be near somebody. The sentence again breaks off into the song without a full stop, exactly as the first one did.

sentences.t:
„Kälbchen, Kälbchen, knie nieder,
vergiß nicht deine Hirtin wieder,
wie der Königssohn die Braut vergaß,
die unter der grünen Linde saß.“
sentences.l:
“Little calf, little calf, kneel down,
forget not your herdswoman again,
as the king’s son forgot the bride
who sat under the green linden.”
sentences.i:
“Little calf, little calf, kneel down,
do not forget your herdswoman,
as the king’s son forgot the bride
who sat beneath the green linden tree.”
sentences.n: The song is repeated word for word, and only its last mark of punctuation changes — a full stop where the first time there was a comma, because this time nothing follows. Sung the first time to a calf, it is aimed the second time at a man on a horse, and he is close enough to hear it.

sentences.t: Als er die Stimme vernahm, blickte er herab und hielt sein Pferd an.
sentences.l: When he heard the voice, he looked down and stopped his horse.
sentences.n: vernehmen is a higher word than hören: to hear, to perceive. anhalten, to stop, splits: hielt … an.

sentences.t: Er schaute der Hirtin ins Gesicht, hielt dann die Hand vor die Augen, als wollte er sich auf etwas besinnen, aber schnell ritt er weiter und war bald verschwunden.
sentences.l: He looked the herdswoman in the face, then held his hand before his eyes, as if he would call something to mind, but he rode quickly on and was soon gone.
sentences.i: He looked the herdswoman in the face, then held his hand before his eyes, as though trying to call something to mind; but he rode quickly on and was soon out of sight.
sentences.n: jemandem ins Gesicht schauen — the dative of possession once more: to look somebody in the face. sich besinnen is to call something to mind, to recollect. He puts his hand before his eyes exactly as the stepmother did on entering the castle, and the tale does not say what he sees.

sentences.t: „Ach,“ sagte sie, „er kennt mich nicht mehr,“ und ihre Trauer ward immer größer.
sentences.l: “Ah,” she said, “he knows me no longer,” and her grief grew ever greater.
sentences.n: kennen is to know a person: er kennt mich nicht mehr, he no longer knows me by sight. immer größer — immer with a comparative makes a steady increase, ever greater.

sentences.t: Bald darauf sollte an dem Hofe des Königs drei Tage lang ein großes Fest gefeiert werden, und das ganze Land ward dazu eingeladen.
sentences.l: Soon after that a great feast was to be held at the king’s court for three days long, and the whole land was invited to it.
sentences.i: Soon afterwards a great feast was to be held at the king’s court for three days, and the whole land was invited to it.
sentences.n: sollte … gefeiert werden is a passive inside a modal: was to be celebrated. drei Tage lang keeps lang after the measure. ward is the old passive auxiliary again.

sentences.t: „Nun will ich das Letzte versuchen“ dachte das Mädchen, und als der Abend kam, gieng es zu dem Stein, unter dem es seine Schätze vergraben hatte.
sentences.l: “Now I will try the last thing,” thought the girl, and when the evening came, she went to the stone under which she had buried her treasures.
sentences.i: “Now I will try the last thing left me,” thought the girl; and when evening came she went to the stone under which she had buried her treasures.
sentences.n: das Letzte is the last thing, an adjective made into a neuter noun. The tale slips back to es and seine for the girl in this sentence, as it does whenever it calls her das Mädchen again.

sentences.t: Sie holte das Kleid mit den goldnen Sonnen hervor, legte es an und schmückte sich mit den Edelsteinen.
sentences.l: She brought out the dress with the golden suns, put it on and adorned herself with the precious stones.
sentences.n: hervorholen, to fetch out, splits: holte … hervor. anlegen here is to put on clothing — legte es an, put it on. The suns come first, then the moons, then the stars, and the order matters: it is in the star dress that he finally speaks to her.

sentences.t: Ihre Haare, die sie unter einem Tuch verborgen hatte, band sie auf, und sie fielen in langen Locken an ihr herab.
sentences.l: Her hair, which she had hidden under a cloth, she unbound, and it fell in long curls down about her.
sentences.i: Her hair, which she had kept hidden under a kerchief, she loosed, and it fell in long curls down about her.
sentences.n: aufbinden here means to untie, to loose — auf as a particle can undo as well as fasten, as in aufmachen, to open. Haare is plural in German where English says hair, hence sie fielen, they fell. herabfallen splits: fielen … herab.

sentences.t: So gieng sie nach der Stadt und ward in der Dunkelheit von niemand bemerkt.
sentences.l: So she went to the town and was noticed by nobody in the darkness.
sentences.i: So she went to the town, and in the darkness nobody noticed her.
sentences.n: von niemand bemerkt — von marks the agent of a passive, by nobody. ward once more for wurde.

sentences.t: Als sie in den hell erleuchteten Saal trat, wichen alle voll Verwunderung zurück, aber niemand wußte wer sie war.
sentences.l: When she stepped into the brightly lit hall, all drew back full of wonder, but nobody knew who she was.
sentences.i: When she stepped into the brightly lit hall, everyone drew back in wonder, but nobody knew who she was.
sentences.n: zurückweichen, to draw back, to give way, splits: wichen … zurück. wußte here is wissen, to know a fact, against kennen, to know a person, in the next sentence but one; German keeps the two apart and English cannot.

sentences.t: Der Königssohn gieng ihr entgegen, doch er erkannte sie nicht.
sentences.l: The king’s son went toward her, yet he did not recognise her.
sentences.n: entgegengehen, to go to meet somebody, takes the dative: gieng ihr entgegen. erkennen is to recognise — the verb the whole tale is waiting on, and it is refused here.

sentences.t: Er führte sie zum Tanz und war so entzückt über ihre Schönheit daß er an die andere Braut gar nicht mehr dachte.
sentences.l: He led her to the dance and was so enraptured over her beauty that he thought no more at all of the other bride.
sentences.i: He led her out to dance and was so enraptured by her beauty that he thought no more at all of the other bride.
sentences.n: entzückt über, delighted at. denken an takes the accusative: an die andere Braut dachte, thought of the other bride. die andere Braut is the false bride of the title, named here in three words and never given a line to speak.

sentences.t: Als das Fest vorüber war, verschwand sie im Gedränge und eilte vor Tagesanbruch in das Dorf, wo sie ihr Hirtenkleid wieder anlegte.
sentences.l: When the feast was over, she vanished in the crush and hurried before daybreak into the village, where she put her herdswoman’s dress on again.
sentences.i: When the feast was over she vanished in the crush and hurried back before daybreak to the village, where she put on her herdswoman’s dress again.
sentences.n: das Gedränge is the press of a crowd. anlegen once more, of clothes: the verb that put the sun dress on takes it off again.

sentences.t: Am andern Abend nahm sie das Kleid mit den silbernen Monden heraus und steckte einen Halbmond von Edelsteinen in ihre Haare.
sentences.l: On the next evening she took out the dress with the silver moons and put a half-moon of precious stones into her hair.
sentences.i: The next evening she took out the dress with the silver moons and set a half-moon of jewels in her hair.
sentences.n: herausnehmen, to take out, splits: nahm … heraus. stecken is to put, to stick a thing into something, and takes the accusative of where it goes: in ihre Haare.

sentences.t: Als sie auf dem Fest sich zeigte, wendeten sich alle Augen nach ihr, aber der Königssohn eilte ihr entgegen, und ganz von Liebe erfüllt tanzte er mit ihr allein und blickte keine andere mehr an.
sentences.l: When she showed herself at the feast, all eyes turned toward her, but the king’s son hurried to meet her, and quite filled with love he danced with her alone and looked at no other woman any more.
sentences.i: When she showed herself at the feast, every eye turned toward her; but the king’s son hurried to meet her, and, filled with love, danced with her alone and looked at no other woman.
sentences.n: sich wenden nach, to turn toward. entgegeneilen, to hurry to meet, takes the dative like entgegengehen. anblicken, to look at, splits: blickte … an.

sentences.t: Ehe sie weggieng, mußte sie ihm versprechen den letzten Abend nochmals zum Fest zu kommen.
sentences.l: Before she went away, she had to promise him to come once more to the feast on the last evening.
sentences.i: Before she went away she had to promise him that she would come to the feast once more on the last evening.
sentences.n: ehe is before, an older and plainer word than bevor. den letzten Abend is a bare accusative of time, on the last evening. weggieng is the 1857 spelling of wegging.

sentences.t: Als sie zum drittenmal erschien, hatte sie das Sternenkleid an, das bei jedem ihrer Schritte funkelte, und Haarband und Gürtel waren Sterne von Edelsteinen.
sentences.l: When she appeared for the third time, she had the star dress on, which sparkled at every one of her steps, and hairband and girdle were stars of precious stones.
sentences.i: When she appeared for the third time she had on the star dress, which sparkled at every step she took, and her hairband and girdle were stars of jewels.
sentences.n: hatte … an is anhaben, to have on, to be wearing, with an at the end. zum drittenmal, for the third time, is printed as one word in 1857. bei jedem ihrer Schritte takes a genitive after jeder: at every one of her steps.

sentences.t: Der Königssohn hatte schon lange auf sie gewartet und drängte sich zu ihr hin.
sentences.l: The king’s son had been waiting for her a long time already and pressed his way to her.
sentences.i: The king’s son had been waiting for her a long time, and pressed his way through to her.
sentences.n: warten auf takes the accusative, to wait for. sich hindrängen, to press one’s way toward, splits: drängte sich … hin. schon lange with a past tense is German for “had been … for a long time”.

sentences.t: „Sage mir nur wer du bist,“ sprach er, „mir ist als wenn ich dich schon lange gekannt hätte.“
sentences.l: “Only tell me who you are,” he said, “it is to me as if I had known you a long time already.”
sentences.i: “Only tell me who you are,” he said, “it seems to me as though I had known you a long time.”
sentences.n: mir ist als wenn is an impersonal turn with no subject: it is to me as if. gekannt hätte is the past subjunctive of kennen, as if I had known you. He is one word from recognising her, and does not.

sentences.t: „Weißt du nicht,“ antwortete sie, „was ich that, als du von mir schiedest?“
sentences.l: “Do you not know,” she answered, “what I did when you parted from me?”
sentences.n: schiedest is the second person past of scheiden, to part, to depart — an old strong form. that is the 1857 spelling of tat. She answers a question with a question, and the answer is an action and not a name.

sentences.t: Da trat sie zu ihm heran und küßte ihn auf den linken Backen: in dem Augenblick fiel es wie Schuppen von seinen Augen und er erkannte die wahre Braut.
sentences.l: Then she stepped up to him and kissed him on the left cheek: in that moment it fell like scales from his eyes and he recognised the true bride.
sentences.i: Then she stepped up to him and kissed him on the left cheek; and in that moment it fell as though scales had dropped from his eyes, and he knew the true bride.
sentences.n: wie Schuppen von den Augen fallen — for scales to fall from the eyes — is a set German phrase for a sudden recognition, and comes from the Acts of the Apostles. wahr in die wahre Braut means true in the sense of real, genuine: the true bride as against the false one waiting at court, not the faithful one. erkennen, to recognise — the verb refused twice at the feast — is granted at last, and a kiss on the cheek does it.

sentences.t: „Komm,“ sagte er zu ihr, „hier ist meines Bleibens nicht länger,“ reichte ihr die Hand und führte sie hinab zu dem Wagen.
sentences.l: “Come,” he said to her, “here is no staying for me any longer,” gave her his hand and led her down to the carriage.
sentences.i: “Come,” he said to her, “there is no staying here for me any longer” — and he gave her his hand and led her down to the carriage.
sentences.n: hier ist meines Bleibens nicht is an old genitive turn: here is nothing of my staying, there is no staying here for me. reichte ihr die Hand — the plain article once more where English wants his hand.

sentences.t: Als wäre der Wind vorgespannt, so eilten die Pferde zu dem Wunderschloß.
sentences.l: As if the wind had been harnessed in front, so the horses hurried to the wonder-castle.
sentences.i: As though the wind had been harnessed in front of them, the horses hurried to the wonder castle.
sentences.n: vorspannen is to harness a beast in front of a carriage, so als wäre der Wind vorgespannt puts the wind itself in the traces. als wäre with a subjunctive and no ob is as if, and German simply inverts the verb.

sentences.t: Schon von weitem glänzten die erleuchteten Fenster.
sentences.l: Already from afar the lighted windows shone.
sentences.n: von weitem, from a distance. The castle stands lit and waiting, and the tale never says who lit it.

sentences.t: Als sie bei der Linde vorbei fuhren, schwärmten unzählige Glühwürmer darin, sie schüttelte ihre Äste und sendete ihre Düfte herab.
sentences.l: When they drove past the linden, countless glow-worms were swarming in it, it shook its branches and sent its scents down.
sentences.i: As they drove past the linden, countless glow-worms swarmed in it; it shook its branches and sent its fragrance down.
sentences.n: sie schüttelte ihre Äste — sie is the linden, feminine in German, so English must say it; the tree is doing this itself. vorbei fuhren is printed as two words here, where the collection elsewhere writes vorbeifuhren. The tree she was told to wait under is the last thing in the tale to greet her.

sentences.t: Auf der Treppe blühten die Blumen, aus dem Zimmer schallte der Gesang der fremden Vögel, aber in dem Saal stand der ganze Hof versammelt und der Priester wartete um den Bräutigam mit der wahren Braut zu vermählen.
sentences.l: On the staircase the flowers were blooming, out of the room rang the song of the strange birds, but in the hall the whole court stood assembled and the priest was waiting to wed the bridegroom to the true bride.
sentences.i: On the staircase the flowers were in bloom, and out of the room rang the song of the foreign birds; but in the hall the whole court stood assembled, and the priest was waiting to wed the bridegroom to the true bride.
sentences.n: The foreign birds are the ones the old woman set in golden cages when she built the castle, and this is the last the tale says of her work. vermählen takes mit for the person married to. The tale ends on die wahre Braut, the words of its title, and never says what became of the other one.

glossary.alte: alt — old; here die Alte, the old woman (the helper of this tale; der Alte would be the old man)
glossary.anlegte: anlegen — put on (clothing) (3rd sg. past; separable, legte … an)
glossary.aufgeben: aufgeben — to set (a task), to impose (infinitive; separable, gibt … auf; elsewhere to give up)
glossary.auflegen: auflegen — to lay on, to impose (infinitive; separable; eine Arbeit auflegen: to set somebody work)
glossary.auftrug: auftragen — set (a task), charged with (3rd sg. past; separable, trug … auf)
glossary.backen: der Backen — cheek (acc. sg.; auf den linken Backen, on the left cheek); not backen, to bake
glossary.band: binden — bound, tied (3rd sg. past; ‘band … in ihr Tuch’ = tied into her cloth; with auf, aufbinden, to loose, to untie); not das Band, a band
glossary.besinnen: besinnen — sich besinnen: to call to mind, to recollect (infinitive)
glossary.bezogen: beziehen — covered, hung (past participle; mit Seide bezogen, hung with silk; also to move into a house)
glossary.drückt: drücken — presses, weighs on (3rd sg. present; ‘was dich drückt’ = what is weighing on you)
glossary.dulde: dulden — I tolerate, I allow (1st sg. present; ich dulde keinen Widerspruch)
glossary.erbarmt: erbarmen — sich erbarmen + genitive: takes pity on (3rd sg. present; der sich meiner erbarmt)
glossary.ergehen: ergehen — to go, to fare (impersonal, + dative: ‘so wird dirs schlimm ergehen’ = then it will go badly with you)
glossary.herde: die Herde — herd, flock (acc. sg.; not der Herd, the hearth, which this tale also uses)
glossary.kennt: kennen — knows, recognises (3rd sg. present; of knowing a person)
glossary.knie: knien — kneel! (2nd sg. imperative: ‘knie nieder’ = kneel down); also das Knie, the knee
glossary.lichtern: das Licht — lights (dat. pl.; der Glanz von tausend Lichtern)
glossary.liebe: die Liebe — love (‘ganz von Liebe erfüllt’ = quite filled with love)
glossary.liebsten: der Liebste — her beloved, her sweetheart (acc. sg.; the adjective lieb used as a noun)
glossary.macht: machen — makes (3rd sg. present; ‘wenn es dir Freude macht’ = if it gives you pleasure)
glossary.mein: mein — my; but in ‘harre mein’ it is the old genitive of ich, of me (harren takes the genitive)
glossary.ruf: der Ruf — report, repute, fame (‘der Ruf gieng durch die Welt’ = word of her went round the world); elsewhere a call, a shout
glossary.rühren: rühren — to stir, to move (infinitive; ‘das Herz rühren’ = to touch the heart)
glossary.sage: sagen — say, tell (2nd sg. imperative: ‘sage mir’ = tell me); not die Sage, a legend
glossary.schnitte: schneiden — cut (3rd sg. past subjunctive, schnitte; als ob ein Messer schnitte: as though a knife were cutting)
glossary.schöpfe: ausschöpfen — scoop out, bail out (2nd sg. imperative; separable, ‘schöpfe … aus’)
glossary.sitz: der Sitz — seat (dat. sg.; erhob sich von ihrem Sitz)
glossary.spiegelten: spiegeln — were mirrored, reflected (3rd pl. past; sich spiegeln in)
glossary.spürte: spüren — searched, nosed about (3rd sg. past; the hunter’s word in an older sense; elsewhere to feel, to sense)
glossary.staunte: staunen — was astonished (3rd sg. past; staunen über: to marvel at)
glossary.stoben: stieben — flew apart, scattered (3rd pl. past of stieben; aus einander stieben: to fly apart)
glossary.tracht: die Tracht — a load, a portion; ‘eine Tracht Schläge’ = a sound beating, a good hiding (elsewhere Tracht is costume, garb)
glossary.versprechen: versprechen — to promise (infinitive; ‘mußte sie ihm versprechen’ = had to promise him); also das Versprechen, a promise
glossary.vornehmen: vornehmen — to take up, to set about (something) (infinitive; separable, nimmt … vor; not the adjective vornehm)
glossary.weiß: wissen — know (1st and 3rd sg. present: ‘ich weiß’, ‘wer weiß’); not weiß, white
